study_identification.title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

study_characteristics.study_objective: Use normative modeling to quantify and map individual-level deviations in brain structure in adults with persistent ADHD relative to normative aging, and compare individual heterogeneity with group-level case–control differences.

deviation_metric.answer: Voxel-wise Z-scores from GPR predictions; extreme deviations thresholded at |Z| > 2.6; participant-level percentage of extreme negative/positive deviations; group-level mean deviation maps (Z) and FDR-corrected contrasts using PALM.
deviation_metric.reason: Methods describe Z-score computation per voxel, thresholding at ±2.6, PALM group-level maps, and summary as percentage of extreme deviations per participant.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: ...computing a Z-score for each voxel... thresholded at |Z| > 2.6... extreme deviations were combined into scores representing the percentage of extreme positive and extreme negative deviations for each participant...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group-level differences assessed via PALM with FDR (5%) using TFCE; participant-level percentages of extreme deviations compared between ADHD and controls using a nonparametric chi-squared test in a GLM; associations with age, symptom scores, stimulant medication, and comorbidity tested with Bonferroni-Holm correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Adults with persistent ADHD show mean gray matter reductions in cerebellum and hippocampus relative to controls, but individual extreme deviations are highly heterogeneous with minimal spatial overlap (>2% of patients in only a few loci).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: ADHD vs controls showed significant mean gray matter deviations in cerebellum, temporal regions, and hippocampus (FDR 5%). Percentage of extreme negative deviations (gray matter): ADHD 0.48% (95% CI 0.30–0.66) vs controls 0.28% (95% CI 0.24–0.34); Wald χ2(1) = 23.64, p_corr < 0.001. White matter: ADHD 0.41% (95% CI 0.24–0.57) vs controls 0.24% (95% CI 0.17–0.31); Wald χ2(1) = 18.02, p_corr < 0.001. Overlap of extreme negative deviations exceeded 2% of patients primarily in cerebellum, hippocampus, and basal ganglia; positive deviations showed scattered patterns.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Different validation strategies for groups due to sample size (10-fold CV in controls vs out-of-sample predictions in ADHD) may introduce bias; self-reported symptom measures are noisier than diagnostic interviews; sample size and heterogeneity precluded detailed analysis of comorbidities and other confounders.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Single-site 1.5T acquisition; normative modeling provides individualized deviation maps complementary to case–control analyses.

general_notes.general_notes: All participants Dutch and of European Caucasian ancestry; MRI on 1.5T Magnetom Avanto with 1 mm isotropic MPRAGE. Group-level maps thresholded at Z = ±2.6 for visualization and FDR-corrected contrasts reported.
